questions.stem: Which number sequence is represented by the number of sides in the sequence of Regular Polygons?
questions.solution: The number of sides in the sequence of Regular Polygons starts from 3 and follows the counting numbers: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, ... The option 'Odd numbers' is incorrect because it starts from 3 but includes even numbers as well. The option 'Even numbers' is incorrect because it excludes odd numbers. The option 'Counting numbers starting from 1' is incorrect because the sequence starts from 3.

questions.solution: The sequence of regular polygons is based on the number of sides, which starts at 3 and increases by 1 for each subsequent polygon. questions.stem: What is the common difference in the sequence of jars arranged in layers, where the top layer has 3 jars, the next has 6, the third has 9, and so on?
questions.solution: The sequence of jars in the layers is 3, 6, 9, ... which is an arithmetic progression. The common difference is the difference between any two consecutive terms. For example, 6 - 3 = 3. Hence, the common difference is 3. The option 6 is the first term, 9 is the third term, and 12 is the fourth term, so they are incorrect.

hi.stem: क्रम में व्यवस्थित जारों की परतों में सामान्य अंतर क्या है, जहां शीर्ष परत में 3 जार हैं, अगली परत में 6 हैं, तीसरी परत में 9 हैं, और इसी तरह आगे बढ़ते जाते हैं?
hi.solution: जारों की परतों का अनुक्रम 3, 6, 9, ... है, जो एक समांतर श्रेढ़ी है। सामान्य अंतर किन्हीं दो क्रमागत पदों के बीच का अंतर होता है। उदाहरण के लिए, 6 - 3 = 3। इसलिए, सामान्य अंतर 3 है। विकल्प 6 प्रथम पद है, 9 तीसरा पद है, और 12 चौथा पद है, इसलिए वे गलत हैं।

questions.stem: If the number of little squares in each shape of the sequence of Stacked Squares forms a sequence, what is the sequence?
questions.solution: The sequence of the number of little squares in each shape of the Stacked Squares is 1, 4, 9, 16, ..., which are perfect squares. Each term in the sequence is the square of its position in the sequence. The other options do not represent square numbers; 1, 2, 3, 4, ... is just counting numbers, 1, 3, 6, 10, ... is triangular numbers, and 1, 2, 4, 8, ... is powers of two.

questions.stem: Which sequence is formed by starting with 1 and adding the counting numbers up?
questions.solution: The sequence formed by starting with 1 and adding the counting numbers up is the triangular number sequence. For example, 1, 1 + 2, 1 + 2 + 3, and so on. The square number sequence is formed by squaring numbers, the cubic number sequence is formed by cubing numbers, and the hexagonal number sequence is a different sequence altogether.
